It is because the amendment moved by the hon. member for Port Arthur applies not just to trucking and one other mode but to any of the modes of transport. If a railway wishes to buy a pipe line, or if a steamship company wants to buy an air line, it would apply equally. It applies to all modes of transport under the jurisdiction of parliament and therefore it seemed appropriate to make it to the clause dealing with the commission. Though we all know it was brought about mainly because of the trucking situation and that it is mainly desired by those in the trucking business, it was thought preferable to make it of general application.

As you know, Mr. Speaker, boards of education fall under the jurisdiction of provincial governments. It is not appropriate for me to deal directly with school boards. I think all negotiations should be carried on through the provincial authorities. To clarify the matter a little further, I think there is no federal responsibility in the field of language training in schools, even for immigrants. As far as adult immigrants are concerned, if they need language training in order to obtain employment opportunities I think we can help financially.

Perhaps the minister will keep himself calm and in his general good humour while I develop my argument. Provincial governments have no access to indirect fields of taxation.
